outcome: Raise the Mermaid editor's code-editing + render loop to viewer-grade reliability and polish, benchmarked against mermaid.live, without regressing performance or the offline posture. Deliver: (1) an isolated, mutually-serialized, leak-free Mermaid render pipeline in src/lib/mermaid.ts whose config-establish + render + cleanup is one atomic critical section against the Mermaid singleton and always restores shared configuration; (2) commit epochs in DiagramPreview so only the newest logical request while still mounted may touch any user-visible surface; (3) non-destructive, diagram-type-scoped retain-and-dim of the last-good diagram on invalid input, with a slim persistent feedback affordance and a full blocking error card reserved for cold-start; (4) a single best-effort Monaco diagnostic marker carrying the complete message with native F8/Shift+F8 navigation, derived from the same debounced render; (5) always-on synchronous context-aware completions and starter snippets for all 20 DiagramType categories, available independent of render success; (6) image/copy export kept enabled against the retained last-good SVG with an honest, non-silent stale warning. Preserve the 300ms debounce, lazy CodeEditor load, Monaco-from-CDN offline posture, DEFAULT_MERMAID_CONFIG + sequence auto-coloring render fidelity, the existing export contract strings/toasts and data-testid contracts, and the verified 127-pass / 2-skip unit baseline.
approach: Two complementary, explicitly-required ordering safeguards operate together, addressing both correctness and the peer-raised concurrency concern that 'ignore stale results' alone does not prevent concurrent Mermaid singleton work. SERIALIZATION (constraint: 'mutually serialize all Mermaid singleton configuration-plus-render work'): a module-level promise-chain mutex in src/lib/mermaid.ts wraps every config-establish + render + cleanup in a single critical section, so no two renders interleave against the shared singleton and every render provably behaves as if executed alone (AC-001). mermaid.initialize is gated on a normalized effective-config key so it is NOT reinitialized per keystroke; rendering targets a detached offscreen container passed as render()'s 3rd argument; a finally block always removes that container plus any orphan #d<id>/#<id> nodes and, on any non-success outcome (throw/reject), re-initializes with the last-good/baseline config — rollback is native because Mermaid's setSiteConfig resets-to-defaultConfig-then-merges on every call, so a bad config never accumulates. COMMIT EPOCHS (a separate ordering safeguard, per constraint): a monotonic render token plus a mounted ref in DiagramPreview mean only the newest logical request, and only while mounted, may commit SVG, diagnostics, markers, export source, last-good, or displayed state; superseded queued renders may additionally short-circuit before doing expensive work, but correctness rests on the token+mount guard. A last-good cache whose content identity is (code, effectiveConfig, svg) — no render ID — enables A→B→A convergence to the newest logical request and reuse only when the cached tuple provably matches the exact current (code, effectiveConfig). On invalid input the last-good SVG is retained and dimmed only when detectDiagramType(currentCode) still matches the retained type (else cleared to cold-start / full blocking card); currentSvgString continues to hold the last VALID render so image/copy export use exactly that SVG with a non-silent stale toast, while copy-code/share/markdown always use the raw current source. Diagnostics come solely from the single debounced render rejection via a centralized extractErrorLocation helper (jison hash.loc → 'Parse/Lexical/Syntax error on line N' regex → hash.line+1 → langium 'offset:N' walked over code → null), threaded onDiagnostic→App→CodeEditor.errorMarker into monaco.editor.setModelMarkers(owner 'mermaid') as at most one best-effort marker whose full message is always visible (precise location when trustworthy, else whole-line-1, never invented). Completions are a synchronous, idempotently-registered Monaco provider fed by a pure, framework-free src/lib/completions.ts (keyword vocabulary from CodeEditor.mermaidLanguageDefinition + starter snippets reusing the e2e-validated DIAGRAM_EXAMPLES), context-aware by first non-comment line with a generic fallback, working regardless of render success. Last-good and diagnostics live in in-memory React state / props (never useLocalStorage outside App.tsx). Do NOT bundle Monaco locally, do NOT add a separate validator/linter/LSP/multi-diagnostic system, do NOT add heavy deps. Viewer polish (cursor-anchored zoom, fit-to-content, prettify) and any persisted settings toggle are explicitly DEFERRED per the editor-focused charter and SCOPE constraint.

steps.title: Establish the rock-solid serialized, config-isolated, leak-free render core in src/lib/mermaid.ts (BASE)
how: Add shared types to src/types/index.ts (prefer `type` for new shapes): `type ErrorLocation = { line: number; column?: number; endColumn?: number }` and `type RenderDiagnostic = { message: string; location: ErrorLocation | null; kind: 'syntax' | 'dependency' }`. Export both.

Add a module-level serialization primitive in src/lib/mermaid.ts: `let renderChain: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();` plus an internal `enqueue<T>(task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` that appends task to renderChain so config-establish + render + cleanup for one call runs as a single atomic critical section (satisfies the mutual-serialization constraint; commit epochs remain a separate safeguard in step-2).

Track module state: `lastAppliedConfigKey: string | null` (normalized JSON of the effective config actually initialized) and `committedConfig: MermaidConfig | null` (last-good config). Add `normalizeConfigKey(config)` producing a stable, order-independent string; reuse it as the cache-identity config key in step-2.

Gate initialization inside the critical section: only call the existing mermaid.initialize(fullConfig) when `normalizeConfigKey(effectiveConfig) !== lastAppliedConfigKey`; update lastAppliedConfigKey on success. Keep the existing DEFAULT/theme 'base'/look/fontFamily/themeVariables merge shape and the isolated `as any` cast.

Render into a detached offscreen container: `const container = document.createElement('div')` styled offscreen (position:absolute; left:-99999px; top:0; visibility:hidden), appended to document.body; call `mermaid.render(id, code, container)` with a unique id, then run postProcessSequenceDiagramSvg on the returned svg.

finally cleanup (ALWAYS runs): remove `container` from the DOM; defensively remove any lingering `document.getElementById('d'+id)` and `document.getElementById(id)` nodes; on any non-success outcome re-initialize Mermaid with `committedConfig` (or the baseline default if none) to restore shared config. Do NOT advance committedConfig here.

Extend the public API without breaking callers: keep `renderMermaid(code, elementId, config)` returning `{ svg }` but route it through enqueue + config-key-gated init + offscreen container + postProcess. Add `setCommittedConfig(config)` (advances committedConfig, called by the successful committer in step-2) and keep the existing `extractErrorMessage` export.

Add `extractErrorLocation(error, code): ErrorLocation | null` implementing the empirically-verified chain: (1) error.hash.loc.first_line/first_column/last_column (jison, precise, 1-based), (2) `/(?:Parse|Lexical|Syntax) error on line (\d+)/i` on the message, (3) error.hash.line + 1 (block 'Lexical error'), (4) `/offset:?\s*(\d+)/i` (langium packet/architecture/pie) converted to {line,column} by walking `code`, (5) null. Best-effort/bounded; never fabricate an unreliable location.

Add `detectDiagramType(code): DiagramType | null` that maps the first non-comment, non-YAML-frontmatter, non-%%{init}%% line to a DiagramType (used for last-good type scoping in step-2). Returns null when no recognizable root directive exists.
Add `isDependencyError(error): boolean` classifying Vite dynamic-import/chunk-load and Mermaid module-init dependency failures vs syntax errors.
Remove the production `console.log` at src/lib/mermaid.ts:83. Keep postProcessSequenceDiagramSvg and validateMermaidSyntax intact.

Do NOT change global src/test/setup.ts mermaid-mock behavior (its `render` is a vi.fn that already ignores the extra container arg, keeping the 127-pass baseline). For serialization-ordering tests, use per-test `vi.mocked(...).mockImplementationOnce` with manually-controllable promises rather than editing the global mock.
verification: New src/lib/mermaid.test.ts: extractErrorLocation across the captured jison ('Parse error on line N' + hash.loc), 'Lexical error on line N' + hash.line, langium 'at offset: N', frontmatter-shifted, and CRLF strings, plus the null fallback; detectDiagramType across representative headers incl. frontmatter/directive/gibberish; isDependencyError true/false; serialization ordering via two overlapping renders with manually-resolved mock promises asserting no interleave and that config is restored after a reject; offscreen-container cleanup asserting document.body has zero orphan render nodes after both success and reject.
Run `npx vitest run src/lib/mermaid.test.ts`, then full `npm run test` (must stay 127 pass / 2 skip plus the new tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run build`.

steps.title: Add commit epochs, type-scoped retain-and-dim, and single-path diagnostics to DiagramPreview
how: Introduce a monotonic `renderTokenRef` incremented on each debounced trigger and a `mountedRef` (true until unmount). Capture the token at dispatch; after the awaited render/cache resolution, commit SVG/diagnostic/last-good/export-source ONLY if `token === renderTokenRef.current && mountedRef.current`. Preserve the existing 300ms debounce and lazy load exactly; keep the skeleton only for cold-start (no last-good, still loading).

Maintain an in-memory last-good cache `{ code, effectiveConfigKey, svg, type }` in a ref/state (NOT useLocalStorage). Content identity excludes any render ID. Reuse a cached result only when it proves the exact current (code, normalizeConfigKey(config)); use this to converge A→B→A to the newest logical request.

On success: setSvg(result.svg), clear diagnostic + isStale, update last-good (code, config key, svg, detectDiagramType(code)), call onSvgRendered(svg) to advance export source, call onDiagnostic(null), and call mermaid.setCommittedConfig(effectiveConfig).

On syntax failure: compute `RenderDiagnostic` via extractErrorLocation; if `detectDiagramType(currentCode)` matches last-good.type, RETAIN the last-good SVG rendered dimmed (~45% opacity) inside the SAME `data-testid='mermaid-diagram'` wrapper so a visible <svg> remains (preserving e2e/test contracts), keep onSvgRendered pointing at the retained last-good SVG, emit onStaleChange(true), and emit onDiagnostic(diagnostic). If the type differs or the root directive was removed, clear last-good and render the full blocking Syntax Error card (cold-start).
On empty source: clear svg, error, diagnostic, marker source, isStale, and last-good; call onSvgRendered('') and onDiagnostic(null) so a subsequent invalid edit shows the full error state.

On dependency failure (isDependencyError): show a dedicated Retry panel (shadcn Alert + Button, @phosphor-icons/react duotone) that re-triggers render; do not clear or block the editor; emit onDiagnostic({kind:'dependency', ...}).

Add a persistent, non-obscuring feedback region (slim shadcn Alert/Badge, low emphasis) plus an `aria-live='polite'` region announcing syntax errors, and an accessible description (aria-label/visually-hidden text) on the retained/dimmed preview stating rendering is paused and the previous valid state is shown.

Extend props (all new ones optional, backward compatible with App's current code/config/onSvgRendered usage): add `onDiagnostic?: (d: RenderDiagnostic | null) => void` and `onStaleChange?: (stale: boolean) => void`; keep the `onSvgRendered` signature unchanged.

Unmount cleanup: set mountedRef=false and clear the debounce timer in the effect teardown so no state/marker/DOM/export commit occurs after unmount; an in-flight uninterruptible Mermaid op still restores config via step-1's finally and cannot commit due to the token+mount guard.
Reserve the full centered error card ONLY for cold-start (no last-good / empty source).
verification: Extend src/components/DiagramPreview.test.tsx: resolve-then-reject retains the last-good svg (svg still present in [data-testid=mermaid-diagram]; onStaleChange(true); onDiagnostic called with a message); a diagram-type change on failure clears last-good (full card); empty source clears everything then a following invalid edit shows the full card; two rapid renders assert only the latest token commits; keep the existing '.diagram-preview-bg' and onSvgRendered assertions passing.
`npm run test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` all green.

steps.title: Wire diagnostics + stale-export state through App.tsx and add honest stale export warning
how: Add App state `diagnostic: RenderDiagnostic | null` and `isExportStale: boolean`, set by DiagramPreview's onDiagnostic/onStaleChange callbacks. Thread `diagnostic` to CodeEditor as a new optional `errorMarker?: RenderDiagnostic | null` prop.

Keep currentSvgString holding the last VALID render (already flows from onSvgRendered), so handleExport/handleCopyImage keep using it unchanged. When isExportStale, after a successful image/PNG/copy-image, additionally emit a low-emphasis toast e.g. `toast.warning('Exported last valid diagram — current source has errors')`; do NOT change the existing 'No diagram to export'/'No diagram to copy' gating strings or the 'Exported as <FMT>'/'Image copied to clipboard' success toasts.
Ensure copy-code, share, and markdown export continue to use the RAW current `code` (unchanged), so they never imply the invalid current source is valid.
Snapshot currentSvgString into a local const at the start of handleExport/handleCopyImage so export cannot race into a later cached result without an explicit user-visible state change.
Do NOT add any useLocalStorage outside App.tsx; pass all new state via props.
verification: App-level/unit coverage where feasible (jsdom): the stale-warning path fires only when isExportStale, and all existing gating strings/toasts are intact; rely on step-6 e2e for the real export-of-retained-SVG proof.
`npm run test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` green; existing export/toast unit tests unchanged.

steps.title: Create the pure, unit-testable completions/snippets library (src/lib/completions.ts)
how: Add src/lib/completions.ts (framework-free, no Monaco import) exporting: keyword vocabulary derived from CodeEditor.mermaidLanguageDefinition arrays (diagramTypes declarations + per-type keyword lists + node-shape/arrow tokens) and `STARTER_SNIPPETS: Record<DiagramType, string>` where each snippet is sourced from the corresponding e2e-validated DIAGRAM_EXAMPLES entry (one working example per DiagramType).

Export `detectContextType(code): DiagramType | null` (first non-comment line) and `buildCompletions(code): { keywords: string[]; snippets: { label: string; insertText: string }[] }` that is context-aware for the detected type with a generic keyword + all-types-snippet fallback for unrecognized/empty input.
Keep completions synchronous and side-effect-free so they are unit-testable and reusable, and available independent of render success.
If the keyword arrays currently live only inside CodeEditor.tsx, export them from there (or move to constants) so both CodeEditor and completions.ts consume one source of truth without duplication.
verification: src/lib/completions.test.ts: for ALL 20 DiagramType categories buildCompletions yields non-empty keywords and ≥1 starter snippet; each snippet equals a real DIAGRAM_EXAMPLES entry (which tests/e2e/diagrams.spec.ts already renders on Mermaid 11.12.2); detectContextType maps representative first-lines correctly; generic fallback returned for gibberish/empty.
`npx vitest run src/lib/completions.test.ts`, full `npm run test`, `npm run lint`.

steps.title: Add the Monaco best-effort marker + idempotent synchronous completion provider to CodeEditor
how: Add the optional `errorMarker?: RenderDiagnostic | null` prop. In an effect keyed on errorMarker + editor readiness, call `monaco.editor.setModelMarkers(model, 'mermaid', [...])` with at most ONE IMarkerData (MarkerSeverity.Error, `message` = the full readable error text, 1-based startLineNumber/startColumn/endColumn from location; when location is null use whole-line-1). Set an empty markers array (clear) when errorMarker is null / on render success — markers derive ONLY from the committed diagnostic so they cannot diverge from the preview (single-path).

Register the completion provider exactly once via a module-level boolean guard inside handleEditorDidMount (CodeEditor is lazy-loaded and StrictMode double-invokes onMount): `monaco.languages.registerCompletionItemProvider('mermaid', { provideCompletionItems(model, position) { return { suggestions } } })` built synchronously from `buildCompletions(model.getValue())`; completions must work regardless of render success.
Do NOT change the existing language registration, Monarch tokenizer, or theme setup — add markers and completions alongside them inside handleEditorDidMount / a marker effect.
Rely on owner-'mermaid' markers so Monaco's native F8 / Shift+F8 diagnostic navigation works unchanged; do NOT intercept F8/Escape (Escape is owned by fullscreen per use-keyboard-shortcuts).
verification: Monaco markers/squiggly/completions cannot run in jsdom → proven by e2e in step-6. Add only a light unit test for prop plumbing / provider-guard idempotency where feasible.
`npm run test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` green.

steps.title: Integration proof (Playwright e2e), documentation, and full verification gate
how: Add tests/e2e/render-resilience.spec.ts (real Monaco + mermaid at :5000): valid→invalid keeps a visible <svg> in [data-testid=mermaid-diagram] (retained + dimmed), a single red .squiggly-error marker appears on the reported line, NO blocking card while last-good exists, document.body has 0 orphan mermaid render nodes after an invalid→valid burst, image/PNG/copy-image stay enabled and emit the stale-warning toast, cold-start (empty then invalid) shows the full Syntax Error card, changing the root diagram directive to a different type clears the retained preview, and F8 navigates the diagnostic.
Add tests/e2e/completions.spec.ts: trigger Ctrl+Space in two diagram contexts and assert context keyword + starter-snippet suggestions appear independent of render state.
Keep tests/e2e/diagrams.spec.ts (already renders+asserts all 20 DiagramType examples on Mermaid 11.12.2 = AC-029 proof) and app/actions specs green.

Docs: add docs/ADR/002-render-pipeline-error-resilience.md (AGENT.md template) documenting serialized config+render + commit epochs, type-scoped retain-and-dim, best-effort single marker, and export-of-retained-SVG semantics; update docs/ARCHITECTURE_GUIDELINES.md §2.1 and docs/AGENT.md for the new DiagramPreview error contract; add a docs/history/ note (blank-on-error → retain-and-dim).

Run the full gate: `npm run lint`, `npm run test`, `npm run build`, and `npm run test:e2e` where runnable. If the e2e chromium/web-server cannot start in the sandbox, ensure specs are lint/type-clean and defer execution proof to CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
verification: All gates green; unit baseline 127 pass / 2 skip preserved with the new mermaid/DiagramPreview/completions tests added in lockstep; e2e render-resilience + completions pass locally or in CI.
e2e/visual check that the retained diagram dims (~45%) and matches mermaid.live-style behavior (retained-dimmed + squiggly, no blocking card, exports enabled).

acceptanceContract: AC-001 isolation: the serialized critical section re-establishes each request's effective config (init gated on config-key change) and renders into a detached offscreen container, so no request observes another's config or DOM and overlapping requests cannot interleave. AC-002/AC-015/AC-026: the queue's finally restores shared config to last-good/baseline on success-not-committed, parse failure, throw, cancel, and unmount; a bad config never advances committedConfig, and an uninterruptible op finishing after unmount still restores config and cannot commit. AC-003/AC-004/AC-005/AC-016: a monotonic render token + mount guard let only the newest logical request commit SVG/diagnostics/markers/export-source/last-good/displayed state; last-good content identity is (code, effectiveConfig, svg) with no render ID, enabling A→B→A convergence and proven-current reuse only. AC-006/AC-009/AC-010: invalid input retains and dims only the most recently committed good code/config/SVG when detectDiagramType still matches, clears incompatible retained output on type/root-directive change, and empties everything on empty source so a later invalid edit shows the full error. AC-007/AC-017/AC-018/AC-027/AC-030: diagnostics derive solely from the single debounced render rejection via extractErrorLocation, surfaced as at most one best-effort owner-'mermaid' marker carrying the complete message (precise location when trustworthy, else whole-line-1, never invented), cleared/replaced on change or success, so markers and preview never diverge. AC-008: with no last-good, invalid input shows the full blocking error card. AC-011/AC-012/AC-013: image export/copy use exactly the retained displayed SVG (post prepareSVGForExport), snapshotted at click, with a non-silent stale warning; copy-code/share/markdown use raw source; export cannot race into a later cache without a user-visible state change. AC-014: unmount cancels pending/debounced/in-flight commits. AC-019/AC-020/AC-021: a slim persistent feedback region never obscures the retained preview, syntax errors announce via aria-live polite, and the dimmed preview exposes an accessible paused/last-valid description. AC-022: owner-'mermaid' markers keep native F8/Shift+F8. AC-023: dependency load failure shows a Retry panel with the editor still functional. AC-024/AC-025: typing is never blocked (300ms debounce + lazy load preserved; skeleton only on cold-start) and no temporary DOM/shared-config leaks after invalid→valid bursts. AC-028/AC-029: synchronous idempotent completions provide keywords + a real DIAGRAM_EXAMPLES-backed starter snippet for all 20 categories independent of render success, and all 20 still render on Mermaid 11.12.2. Gates: npm run lint, npm run test (127 pass / 2 skip preserved, updated tests in lockstep), npm run build, and npm run test:e2e where runnable, all green.

testStrategy: Pure logic is unit-tested with Vitest+jsdom against stable seams: extractErrorLocation over the exact captured jison ('Parse error on line N' + hash.loc), 'Lexical error on line N' + hash.line, langium 'at offset: N', frontmatter-shifted, and CRLF strings plus the null fallback; detectDiagramType; isDependencyError; serialization ordering via two overlapping renders with per-test manually-resolved mock promises (asserting no interleave and config restored after a reject); offscreen-container cleanup via document.body DOM assertions; last-good retention via resolve-then-reject in DiagramPreview; and buildCompletions across all 20 DiagramType categories. Because jsdom cannot exercise real Mermaid parsers ('DOMPurify.addHook is not a function' for class/mindmap) or Monaco, marker squiggles, real error lines, DOM-leak absence, completions, and export-of-retained-SVG are proven only by Playwright e2e at :5000 (render-resilience.spec.ts, completions.spec.ts), with the existing diagrams.spec.ts validating all 20 snippets render on Mermaid 11.12.2. The global src/test/setup.ts mermaid mock is left behavior-unchanged (its render vi.fn already ignores the extra container arg, keeping the 127-pass/2-skip baseline); ordering control is done via per-test overrides. The existing DiagramPreview error test asserts only '.diagram-preview-bg', so retain-and-dim does not break it.
risks: Serialization could add latency if many renders queue; mitigated by the 300ms debounce (typically one render in flight), config-key-gated init, and optional short-circuit of superseded queued renders.

Frontmatter/%%{init}%% directives shift Mermaid-reported lines vs editor lines; the standard is best-effort bounded placement with the full message always visible (optional directive/frontmatter offset correction is deferred, not required for v1).

Playwright e2e may not run in the build sandbox (chromium/web-server on :5000); if so, keep specs lint/type-clean and defer execution proof to CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml), where diagrams.spec.ts and unit tests still cover the inventory and pure logic.
StrictMode double-mount / lazy load could duplicate the Monaco completion provider; mitigated by a module-level idempotent registration guard.
Extracting the keyword vocabulary out of CodeEditor for reuse in completions.ts risks accidental duplication/drift; mitigated by a single exported source of truth consumed by both.
openQuestions: Can the Playwright e2e suite (chromium + web server on :5000) actually run in the build sandbox, or must render-resilience/completions specs be validated only for lint/type-cleanliness with execution proof deferred to CI? (Non-blocking: unit tests + existing diagrams.spec.ts still cover pure logic and the 20-snippet inventory.)
deferredByDesign: Viewer polish: cursor-anchored zoom, true fit-to-content, auto-fit-on-new-diagram (they touch export/screenshot stability and the e2e-visible 100% default) — deferred per the editor-focused charter and SCOPE constraint.
Formatter/prettify and any persisted editor-settings toggle for autocomplete — completions ship always-on to keep scope tight.
Optional frontmatter/%%{init}%% marker line-offset correction — accept known imprecision + always-visible full message for v1.
Bundling Monaco locally — rejected: contradicts the documented offline-after-initial-load + external-CDN-permitted posture and the no-heavy-deps perf budget.
